baseline.comparison: Same calendar period only: a season is compared with that season in every baseline year.

classes.rationale: inside the central 80% of the baseline and |z| < 1
outside the central 80% of the baseline, or 1 standard deviation

percentileMethod: Mid-rank plotting position: P = 100 x (k + t/2 + 1/2) / (n + 1), where k baseline values are below the observation and t are equal to it. With n = 30 the percentile moves in steps of about 3.2 points and cannot exceed 98.4 or fall below 1.6, so an 'extreme' class needs z >= 2.

composite.rule: The period's rainfall total is the anchor: if it is normal, the composite is normal (daily components are shown, but one daily outlier cannot create a class). If the total is above or below normal, its class stands, except that 'extreme' needs at least one other counted component on the same side (otherwise it is capped at 'unusually'). If any other counted component points to the opposite side at least one class away from normal, the composite is normal and marked conflicting. Mean daily intensity (total / days) is reported but never counted: within one calendar period it is the total divided by a constant.

rules.rule: Seasonal temperature unusually high (P > 95 or z >= 1.5).
Seasonal temperature extreme, or unusually high in 2+ consecutive assessed seasons.
Monsoon rainfall at or below P10 and longest monsoon dry spell unusually high.
Dry watch conditions in two consecutive monsoons.
Monsoon rainfall at or above P90, in a location exposed to a flood region.
Monsoon rainfall at or above P95 and very-heavy-rain days (calendar year) unusually high.
Monsoon rainfall at or above P90, in a location exposed to a landslide region.
Monsoon rainfall at or above P95 and very-heavy-rain days (calendar year) unusually high.
Linked fire driver and one of: pre-monsoon temperature above normal, pre-monsoon rainfall below normal.
Linked fire driver, pre-monsoon temperature above normal and pre-monsoon rainfall below normal.
Linked basin sea-warmth driver at or above the percentile typical of past high-cyclone years.
